tdd.title: Test-Driven Development at OZ-POS
tdd.subtitle: Every bug fix, feature, and refactor starts with a failing test.
tdd.description: OZ-POS follows a disciplined 7-phase TDD workflow that makes bugs reproducible before they are fixed, keeps every fix attached to a regression test, and produces small, reviewable, well-documented commits.

phases.title: Analyze
phases.description: Read the relevant code and its callers, note what is untested, and pick the smallest valuable slice — one behavior, one error path, one invariant.

phases.title: Find Weaknesses
phases.description: Spot concrete problems with evidence: failing tests, logs, audit findings, or code review comments. Reproduce the weakness in a test before touching any code.

phases.title: Red
phases.description: Write the smallest failing test that expresses the desired behavior. Confirm it fails for the right reason — the assertion, not a compile error.

phases.title: Green
phases.description: Write the minimal code that makes the test pass. No gold-plating, no speculative generality. Follow the layer conventions: Money in i64 minor units, rusqlite transactions, thiserror errors.

phases.title: Refactor
phases.description: Clean up with the safety net on. Remove duplication, rename for clarity, extract helpers. The test must stay green. Run cargo fmt.

phases.title: Verify
phases.description: Confirm the fix and no regressions, scoped to the changed area. Use test-tdd.sh, test-changed.sh, clippy, and fmt. Full check.sh only before push.

phases.title: Commit
phases.description: Small, focused, well-described while context is fresh. Conventional Commits, one behavior per commit, with a journal entry recording the why.

goldenRules.rule: Test first. Never write implementation code without a failing test in flight.
goldenRules.why: The test is the specification. Without Red first, Green proves nothing.
A one-behavior cycle is fast, reviewable, and bisectable. Big changes are many small TDD cycles.

goldenRules.rule: Every fix ships with its regression test.
goldenRules.why: The test is the only durable record of the bug. No test, no fix.
A failing test, a log line, or an audit entry is evidence. I think this is slow is not.

goldenRules.rule: Journal, docs, and commit while context is fresh.
goldenRules.why: The 20-minute-old-you knows why the code is the way it is. Record it before it evaporates.
The skill ends at commit. The human pushes.

tools.name: test-tdd.sh
tools.description: Fast loop for one crate. Watch mode re-runs tests on every .rs change using the profile.tdd speed profile.

tools.name: test-changed.sh
tools.description: Runs tests only for crates whose files changed vs origin/main. Catches regressions fast.

tools.name: test-ui-changed.sh
tools.description: vitest --changed, only UI tests affected by changed files.

tools.name: cargo nextest
tools.description: Parallel test runner with automatic fail-fast, retries, and structured output.

layers.location: mod tests at the bottom of each module
layers.convention: Every new module needs at least 1 unit test. Tests may use unwrap freely. DB tests use transactions and assert atomicity.

layers.location: ui/src/__tests__, one test file per component
layers.convention: Use localized ids, assert on rendered output, not implementation details.
Contract tests pin the IPC wire shape between Rust and TypeScript.
Every driver needs a mandatory mock for testing. CI fails without it.
